chapters.1.lds: The 2026 lesson connects unfaithfulness with a broken covenant relationship. How does the closing promise reverse the children’s names?
chapters.1.summary: The LORD’s word comes to Hosea in the days of King Jeroboam of Israel. God tells him to marry an unfaithful woman, since the land is unfaithful. He marries Gomer, and she has three children. The first is named Jezreel, for blood shed there. The second is named “No Mercy.” The third is named “Not My People.” Yet Israel will one day be as many as the sand. Where they were called “not my people,” they will be called God’s children.
chapters.2.lds: The lesson studies renewed belonging through God’s love and mercy. What words define the renewed relationship after the threats?
chapters.2.summary: God speaks of Israel as a wife who has gone after other lovers. She thinks they gave her bread, wool, oil, and drink. She does not know that God gave her the grain and the wine. He will block her path and take back his gifts. Then he will lead her into the desert and speak kindly to her. She will call him “my husband.” He will betroth her to himself forever. He will say to “Not My People,” “You are my people.”
chapters.3.lds: The lesson invites readers to consider God’s continued invitation to return. What details remain unknown about the unnamed woman?
chapters.3.summary: The LORD tells Hosea to love a woman again, though she is unfaithful. This is how the LORD loves Israel, who turn to other gods. Hosea buys her for silver and barley. He tells her to stay with him many days and belong to no other man. He will wait for her in the same way. Israel too will live many days without king or sacrifice. Afterward they will return and seek the LORD and David their king.
chapters.4.lds: Why does the speech refuse to blame daughters alone?
chapters.4.summary: The LORD brings a charge against the people of the land. There is no truth, kindness, or knowledge of God. There is cursing, lying, murder, theft, and adultery. The land mourns, and even the animals waste away. God’s dispute is with the priests. His people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. The priests feed on the people’s sin. God will not punish the daughters, since the men themselves go to prostitutes.
chapters.5.lds: Why can Assyria not cure the wound described here?
chapters.5.summary: God calls the priests, the people, and the royal house to listen. They have been a trap for others. Their deeds will not let them return to God. They will seek the LORD with flocks and not find him. Judah’s leaders are like men who move boundary stones. God is like a moth to Ephraim and like rot to Judah. Ephraim saw its sickness and sent to the king of Assyria. He cannot heal them, and God will wait until they seek him.
chapters.6.lds: The lesson connects mercy with sincere devotion beyond outward religious acts. How do charges of violence challenge the opening promises?
chapters.6.summary: The people say, “Let’s return to the LORD.” He has torn them, and he will heal them. He will revive them and come like the spring rain. God answers by asking what he can do with them. Their love is like a morning cloud and like dew that soon vanishes. He desires mercy and not sacrifice. He wants knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. Instead they have broken the covenant, and priests murder on the road.
chapters.7.lds: What dangers do the oven and dove reveal?
chapters.7.summary: God would heal Israel, but its guilt keeps coming to light. Thieves break in, and bands raid outside. The people do not consider that God remembers. Plotters are like an oven that smolders all night and blazes at dawn. All their kings have fallen, and none calls on God. Ephraim is like a cake baked on one side. Ephraim is like a silly dove, calling to Egypt and flying to Assyria. God will spread his net over them.
chapters.8.lds: Why does naming the craftsman matter for the calf?
chapters.8.summary: A trumpet warns that an enemy is coming like an eagle. Israel cries that it knows God, yet it has rejected what is good. The people set up kings without asking God. They made idols of silver and gold. God rejects the calf of Samaria. A workman made it, and it is not God. They sow the wind and will reap the whirlwind. Israel has forgotten its Maker and built palaces.
chapters.9.lds: How does lost land affect worship as well as food?
chapters.9.summary: Hosea tells Israel not to rejoice at the harvest. The people have been unfaithful on every threshing floor. They will not stay in the LORD’s land. They will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria. They will have no offerings to bring on feast days. The days of reckoning have come. The people call the prophet a fool and the inspired man mad. Their children will be lost, and they will wander among the nations.
chapters.10.lds: What would a different harvest require from the people?
chapters.10.summary: Israel is a spreading vine that bears much fruit. The more it prospered, the more altars it built. Its heart is divided. The calf of Bethel will be carried to Assyria as a gift. Samaria’s king will vanish like a twig on water. God tells them to sow righteousness and reap kindness. They must break up their unplowed ground and seek the LORD. Instead they have plowed wickedness and trusted in their soldiers.
chapters.11.lds: How does the lion’s role change at the end?
chapters.11.summary: God says he loved Israel as a child and called his son out of Egypt. The more he called, the more they went away. He taught Ephraim to walk and carried them in his arms. He bent down and fed them. Now they refuse to return, and the sword will come. Then God asks how he can give them up. His heart turns over, and his compassion grows warm. He will roar like a lion, and his children will come trembling home.
chapters.12.lds: How do memories of Jacob challenge dishonest wealth?
chapters.12.summary: Ephraim chases the wind and makes treaties with Assyria and Egypt. The LORD has a charge against Judah and Jacob. In the womb Jacob grasped his brother’s heel. As a man he struggled with God, wept, and asked for favor. So the people must turn to their God. They must keep kindness and justice and wait for him. A merchant with false scales loves to cheat. Ephraim says its wealth proves it has done no wrong.
chapters.13.lds: Why does remembered care make forgetfulness more serious?
chapters.13.summary: Ephraim once spoke and others trembled, but he died through Baal. Now the people make silver idols and kiss calves. They will vanish like morning mist. Yet the LORD has been their God since Egypt. He cared for them in the desert. When they were fed, they grew proud and forgot him. So he will meet them like a lion and a bear. Their kings cannot save them, and Samaria will bear its guilt.
chapters.14.lds: The lesson studies freely given love and the blessings of repentance. How do the plant pictures reverse earlier losses?
chapters.14.summary: Hosea calls Israel to return to the LORD. He tells them to bring words with them. They should ask God to forgive and accept their praise. They should say that Assyria cannot save them. They will not trust horses or call their handmade things gods. God says he will heal them and love them freely. He will be like dew to Israel. Israel will blossom like a lily and spread like an olive tree.
